The test `['pandas.tests.indexes.datetimes.test_setops.TestBusinessDatetimeIndex.test_intersection_bug()']` failed.
The test looks like:

```python
467 :     def test_intersection_bug(self):
468 :         # GH #771
469 :         a = bdate_range("11/30/2011", "12/31/2011")
470 :         b = bdate_range("12/10/2011", "12/20/2011")
471 :         result = a.intersection(b)
472 :         tm.assert_index_equal(result, b)
473 :         assert result.freq == b.freq # error occurred here
```

It failed with the following error message and call stack:

```
E       AssertionError: assert None == <BusinessDay>
E        +  where None = DatetimeIndex(['2011-12-12', '2011-12-13', '2011-12-14', '2011-12-15',\n               '2011-12-16', '2011-12-19', '2011-12-20'],\n              dtype='datetime64[ns]', freq=None).freq
E        +  and   <BusinessDay> = DatetimeIndex(['2011-12-12', '2011-12-13', '2011-12-14', '2011-12-15',\n               '2011-12-16', '2011-12-19', '2011-12-20'],\n              dtype='datetime64[ns]', freq='B').freq
>       assert result.freq == b.freq
pandas/tests/indexes/datetimes/test_setops.py:473: AssertionError
```

Start by calling the `get_covered_packages` function.

Conclusion: The failing test `pandas.tests.indexes.datetimes.test_setops.TestBusinessDatetimeIndex.test_intersection_bug` checks whether the intersection method correctly preserves the frequency of a DatetimeIndex. However, it fails with an AssertionError because the frequency attribute of the resulting index is not equal to that of the second input index 'b'. This occurs due to `result.freq` being None while 'b.freq' is '<BusinessDay>'. The issue lies in the intersection method not preserving the frequency when intersecting DatetimeIndex objects.
